event: East India Company man Robert Addams writes of drinking 'punch' in India (28 Sept) - earliest known English mention.
significance: Punch (spirit, citrus, sugar, water, spice) is the ancestor of every tiki drink.

event: England captures Jamaica; rum gradually becomes the Royal Navy's spirit ration.
significance: Ties rum to the navy and the Caribbean sugar economy.

event: Mount Gay's oldest surviving estate deed in Barbados (brand's claimed founding date).
significance: Barbados is often called rum's birthplace; its balanced blended style is a tiki 'bridge' rum.

event: Admiral Edward Vernon's Captain's Order No. 349 (21 Aug) cuts the rum ration with water; sugar and lime allowed.
significance: Birth of grog - rum, water, lime, sugar - and the template for Don's Navy Grog.

event: Appleton Estate in Jamaica dates its sugar and rum operation to this year.
significance: Jamaican pot-still rum supplies the funk and body of classic tiki blends.

event: J. Wray & Nephew is established in Kingston, Jamaica.
significance: Its 17-year rum became the base of Trader Vic's 1944 Mai Tai.

event: Facundo Bacardí Massó founds Bacardi in Santiago de Cuba.
significance: Popularizes the light, filtered Spanish-Caribbean style used as a tiki 'backbone' rum.

event: London's Fun magazine prints a rhyming 'Planter's Punch' recipe: 1 sour, 2 sweet, 3 strong, 4 weak (by glass).
significance: Earliest known rhymed ratio recipe for the punch balance tiki still uses.

event: John D. Taylor's Velvet Falernum is established in Barbados (brand's claimed date).
significance: Falernum - lime, clove, ginger, almond - becomes a core tiki spice liqueur.

event: New York Times (8 Aug) prints the Planter's Punch verse: 2 sour, 1.5 sweet, 3 strong ('Old Jamaica'), 4 weak.
significance: Source of the famous sour-sweet-strong-weak mnemonic.

event: Constantino Ribalaigua Vert is tending bar at El Floridita, Havana.
significance: The 'cocktail king' refines rum, lime and sugar into precise Daiquiri variations.

event: Hawaii pavilion at San Francisco's Panama-Pacific Exposition sparks a mainland Hawaiian music craze.
significance: Early seed of the American South Seas fantasy.

event: Ribalaigua buys El Floridita.
significance: Floridita becomes the 'cradle of the Daiquiri' and a model of tropical bar precision.

event: U.S. Prohibition begins (17 Jan); drinkers and bartenders head to Havana.
significance: Cuban cocktail tourism shows Americans that a bar can be the destination.

event: Ernest Raymond Beaumont Gantt (future Donn Beach) leaves home to travel the Caribbean and South Pacific.
significance: His travels supply the drinks, props and persona of the first tiki bar.

event: Royal Hawaiian Hotel ('Pink Palace') opens in Waikiki for Matson Line passengers.
significance: Luxury Hawaii tourism; later home of the 1953 Royal Hawaiian Mai Tai.

event: Don's Beachcomber Café opens at 1722 N. McCadden Place, Hollywood (some date it 5 Dec 1933, others 1934).
significance: The first tiki bar: rum 'Rhum Rhapsodies' in a South Seas fantasy room. Opening year contested.

event: Repeal of Prohibition (5 Dec).
significance: Legal rum returns to U.S. bars just as Don's opens.

event: Donn creates the Zombie in late 1934 (hangover-cure legend; two per customer).
significance: The archetypal three-rum, multi-spice tiki drink.

event: Victor Bergeron opens Hinky Dink's at San Pablo Ave & 65th St, Oakland (17 Nov).
significance: The bar that became Trader Vic's.

event: Don moves across the street to 1727 N. McCadden, renames it Don the Beachcomber and adds Cantonese food.
significance: Sets the Polynesian-restaurant formula: exotic rum drinks plus Chinese-American food.

event: Donn Beach marries Cora Irene 'Sunny' Sund.
significance: Sunny becomes the business mind behind the Beachcomber chain.

event: Dick Santiago is hired at Don the Beachcomber; his pocket recipe notebook dates from these years.
significance: The notebook later lets Jeff Berry decode the original 1934 Zombie.

event: Bergeron visits Havana and Don the Beachcomber, then reworks Hinky Dink's as Trader Vic's (some say 1938).
significance: The second founding house of tiki; renaming date slightly contested.

event: Waring blender comes into bar use, displacing spindle mixers (late 1930s).
significance: Enables frozen/blended drinks; Don's flash-blending used the earlier spindle mixers.

event: A Zombie copy is poured at Monte Proser's Hurricane Bar at the New York World's Fair.
significance: Makes the Zombie a national craze.

event: Donn and Sunny divorce; Sunny keeps mainland rights and grows the chain to about 16 locations.
significance: Don the Beachcomber becomes America's first themed restaurant chain.

event: Don the Beachcomber's Navy Grog appears (c. 1941).
significance: Three rums, lime, grapefruit, honey and soda, served around an ice cone.

event: Donn Beach, USAAF officer, sets up rest camps for 12th and 15th Air Force airmen (Capri, Riviera, Venice); earns Bronze Star.
significance: War service later shapes aviation-named drinks and his move to Hawaii.

event: Trader Vic creates the Mai Tai with 17-year J. Wray & Nephew rum; Carrie Guild exclaims 'Maita'i roa ae!'
significance: The most famous tiki drink; origin disputed by Donn Beach.

event: Tonga Room opens in the Fairmont San Francisco's former swimming pool.
significance: A lasting tiki temple, with a floating band and simulated storms.

event: Trader Vic's Book of Food and Drink is published.
significance: Vic's first book; spreads his recipes to home cooks and drinkers.

event: Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide is published.
significance: Standard bar manual that puts tropical drinks next to the classics.

event: Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki raft sails about 101 days from Peru to the Tuamotus.
significance: A worldwide sensation that fuels South Seas romanticism.

event: James Michener publishes Tales of the South Pacific (Pulitzer 1948).
significance: WWII Pacific stories feed the postwar island fantasy.

event: Donn Beach opens a Don the Beachcomber in Waikiki after the war (c. 1947).
significance: Beach brings his style to Hawaii, since the mainland rights belong to Sunny.

event: South Pacific opens on Broadway.
significance: Rodgers and Hammerstein make the South Seas mainstream.

event: Trader Vic's first franchise, the Outrigger, opens in Seattle's Benjamin Franklin Hotel.
significance: Start of Vic's hotel-partnership growth model.

event: Kon-Tiki's English edition and Heyerdahl's documentary film are released.
significance: 'Kon-Tiki' becomes a brand name for Pacific adventure.

event: Les Baxter releases Ritual of the Savage, including 'Quiet Village'.
significance: Founding album of Exotica music.

event: Trader Vic's opens at 20 Cosmo Place, San Francisco.
significance: Vic's society flagship in the city.

event: Matson hires Trader Vic to create the Royal Hawaiian and Moana hotels' drinks; the Mai Tai reaches Hawaii.
significance: Birth of the 'island' Mai Tai; whether it had pineapple juice is contested.

event: Stephen Crane opens The Luau in Beverly Hills.
significance: Leads to his Kon-Tiki restaurant chain in Sheraton hotels.

event: Caribe Hilton (San Juan) credits Ramón 'Monchito' Marrero with the Piña Colada.
significance: One of several contested Piña Colada origin claims.

event: Conrad Hilton opens a Trader Vic's in the Beverly Hilton.
significance: Hilton partnership takes Vic's global.

event: Oceanic Arts is founded in Whittier, CA, by LeRoy Schmaltz and Bob Van Oosting.
significance: Main supplier of tiki carvings and decor for restaurants and theme parks.

event: Donn Beach creates the International Market Place in Waikiki, with a treehouse office in a banyan.
significance: His Hawaiian showcase; Martin Denny and Don Ho perform there.

event: Mai-Kai opens in Fort Lauderdale (28 Dec) under Bob and Jack Thornton; Mariano Licudine runs the bar.
significance: Keeps Don-style recipes alive for decades.

event: Harry Yee creates the Blue Hawaii at the Hawaiian Village hotel for Bols.
significance: Emblem of the sweeter, colorful resort style; Yee popularizes parasols and orchids.

event: Martin Denny releases the album Exotica, with bird calls; Trader Vic's opens in Chicago's Palmer House.
significance: Exotica names the genre (No. 1 in 1959); Vic's chain spreads through Hilton.

event: Arthur Lyman releases Taboo; Stephen Crane's Kon-Tiki chain expands in Sheraton hotels (late 1950s).
significance: Peak of Exotica and of the Polynesian restaurant chains.

event: Hawaii becomes the 50th state (21 Aug); jet service to Honolulu begins.
significance: Mass tourism turns Waikiki resort drinks into the public face of tiki.

event: Kahiki Supper Club opens in Columbus, Ohio.
significance: Among the grandest Polynesian palaces of the Midwest (closed 2000).

event: Ray Buhen, one of Don's original bartenders, opens Tiki-Ti on Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles.
significance: A direct, family-run link to Beachcomber technique that is still open.

event: Walt Disney's Enchanted Tiki Room opens at Disneyland (23 June).
significance: Brings tiki imagery to children and families; first Audio-Animatronics show.

event: Barrachina restaurant (Old San Juan) claims Ramón Portas Mingot created the Piña Colada.
significance: A rival to the Caribe Hilton claim.

event: Mai Tai dispute: Vic sues Sun-Vac, licensee of Don the Beachcomber mixes; settled in Vic's favor.
significance: Settles the 'official' credit for the Mai Tai.

event: Henry Africa's opens in San Francisco, widely called the first fern bar.
significance: Fern bars and sweet drinks take tiki's place as the fun night out.

event: Royal Navy abolishes the daily rum ration (31 July, 'Black Tot Day').
significance: Ends the 230-year grog tradition.

event: Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide, Revised is published; the Oakland original moves to Emeryville.
significance: Vic restates his Mai Tai claim in print.

event: Jeffrey Ong's Jungle Bird debuts as the Kuala Lumpur Hilton's welcome drink (long misdated to 1978).
significance: Jungle Bird is later revived by Berry and craft bartenders.

event: Puerto Rico names the Piña Colada its official drink.
significance: Cements the Caribe Hilton/Barrachina drink as the island's calling card.

event: Rupert Holmes's 'Escape (The Piña Colada Song)' becomes a hit.
significance: Peak of the commercial 'umbrella drink' image.

event: Victor 'Trader Vic' Bergeron dies (11 Oct).
significance: End of an era for the founding generation.

event: Donn Beach dies in Honolulu (7 June).
significance: The founder dies just before the revival rediscovers him.

event: Otto von Stroheim launches the zine Tiki News.
significance: Connects the collector community behind the tiki revival.

event: Martinique rhum agricole receives AOC status.
significance: Protected cane-juice rhum; agricole becomes a staple of revival rum blending.

event: Jeff Berry publishes Beachbum Berry's Grog Log.
significance: Starts the recovery of authentic golden-age recipes.

event: Sven Kirsten's The Book of Tiki (Taschen) is published.
significance: Names and catalogs Polynesian Pop; makes 'tiki' the umbrella term.

event: Kahiki Supper Club closes and is demolished.
significance: A symbolic loss that energizes preservation-minded fans.

event: Phoebe Beach and Arnold Bitner publish Don the Beachcomber recipes, restating Donn's 1933 Mai Tai claim.
significance: Keeps the Mai Tai dispute alive.

event: Tiki Oasis weekender begins (early 2000s), organized by Otto von Stroheim.
significance: Becomes the scene's biggest annual gathering.

event: Berry's Intoxica! is published, reviving obscure drinks such as the Jungle Bird.
significance: Expands the rediscovered canon.

event: Wray & Nephew finds a barrel remnant and a few unmarked bottles of its 17-year rum.
significance: Relics of the original Mai Tai rum.

event: Jennifer Santiago brings Berry her father Dick's 1930s Beachcomber recipe notebook.
significance: Key to decoding the 1934 Zombie.

event: Martin Cate opens Forbidden Island in Alameda, CA.
significance: Cate's first bar; craft tiki in a classic setting.

event: Berry's Sippin' Safari publishes the decoded 1934 Zombie; Kirsten's Tiki Modern appears.
significance: Landmark recovery of Don's recipes and coded mixes.

event: Haus Alpenz launches St. Elizabeth Allspice Dram in the U.S.
significance: Ends a decades-long gap in pimento dram availability.

event: Smuggler's Cove opens in San Francisco (Dec); Smith & Cross Jamaican rum reaches the U.S.
significance: Sets the template for modern craft tiki bars; brings back high-ester Jamaican rum.

event: Paul McGee opens Three Dots and a Dash in Chicago; Berry publishes Potions of the Caribbean.
significance: Tiki goes big-city mainstream; the Caribbean roots are documented.

event: Jeff Berry opens Latitude 29 in New Orleans' French Quarter.
significance: The leading historian runs a working bar.

event: Lost Lake opens in Chicago (Paul McGee, Shelby Allison).
significance: Lighter, more contemporary tropical design.

event: Smuggler's Cove book introduces a production-based rum classification; Plantation OFTD launches; Bacardí 151 discontinued.
significance: Recipes call for rum categories, not brands, protecting them from discontinued rums.

event: Appleton Estate releases the limited 17 Year Old 'Legend', evoking the lost Wray & Nephew 17.
significance: A modern nod to the original Mai Tai rum.

event: Shannon Mustipher publishes Tiki: Modern Tropical Cocktails.
significance: Foregrounds the Caribbean roots and a broader rum perspective.

event: The Mai-Kai closes after a roof collapse; the industry debates tiki's cultural appropriation; Plantation announces a rename.
significance: Start of the 'reckoning' and 'tropical' reframing.

event: Berry and Ed Hamilton release a Zombie rum blend.
significance: Modern products fill gaps left by lost rums.

event: Garret Richard and Ben Wald publish Tropical Standard; Plantation's new name, Planteray, is revealed.
significance: 'Tropical' reframing plus modern technique; rum brand drops colonial language.

event: The restored Mai-Kai reopens in Fort Lauderdale (reported late 2024).
significance: A surviving 1956 tiki temple returns.
